items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: When I studied with Roy – when I played for Roy, Roy said, “I can’t teach you anything on the drums. I’m going to get you on the mallets and tympani.”

ctx.x: Started giving you lessons? Snare drum lessons, I imagine? Or full kit? Bass drum? Anything else other than . . .?
Snare drum first. A parade drum too, at that, because he believed in going up through the ranks. That don’t spoil me, by giving me a brand new set of drums. He could

have got me a set for nothing. He said, “No. You can work for it.” So I had a parade with gut snares in the bottom. You know what that means. Mistakes come out loud and clear. When I studied with Roy – when I played for Roy, Roy said, “I can’t teach you anything on the drums. I’m going to get you on the mallets and tympani.”
